headline: Downing Street says there is no evidence so far of data loss in the DWP incident and cannot rule out a malicious actor.
summary: Update. Re-read DWP's GOV.UK notice (s001) at about 8:09 AM ET: unchanged, still published 27 November with no update line and no return time, so service stays down (c002) and q004 stays open. The BBC live page (s006, entries to 12:56 GMT) and report (s002): at a 12:16 GMT briefing the prime minister's official spokesperson called it a live and ongoing incident, said it was detected on Nov 26 and services were taken down as a precaution, that an investigation is looking at who is behind it and a malicious actor cannot be ruled out (c013, new; t004, t005), and that there is currently no evidence of customer data loss (c014, new; q005 stays open, as DWP and the ICO have not said). Some Universal Credit claimants told the BBC their payments had not arrived, and DWP had not responded (c015, new; t006; c003 detail, q002 answer and who_is_affected updated). headline: DWP's pensions, Universal Credit and PIP online services were still down at midday; whether a hack caused it is still not known.
summary: Update. Re-read DWP's GOV.UK notice (s001) at about 7:12 AM ET: unchanged since first published at 08:11 GMT (some online services offline as a precaution after a cyber incident; working with the NCSC; payments not affected); no return time, so service stays down (c002) and q004 and q005 stay open. The BBC rewrote its report (s002): as of around 12:00 GMT the online systems for pensions, Universal Credit and PIP applications and Tell Us Once still could not be accessed (c005 updated; timeline t003), and Downing Street said there was no evidence a malicious actor is targeting other departments (c010, new). The BBC's live page (s006, new) says services for applying for the State Pension are also down, that it is not clear whether it was a hack or a technical failure and that there is no evidence at this stage of a breach by hackers (c011, new); it says gov.uk problem reports on Downdetector rose from about 7:20 PM GMT on Nov 26, not clearly related. The Register says DWP declined to comment beyond its statement. Theory sweep: read the Hacker News thread on the BBC live page (s007, 43 comments) whole; commenters raise an ordinary cause (old systems, a supplier, human error) and a link to rumours of a cryptography breakthrough, recorded as q007 and q008, both Not established (c012). The earlier Hacker News thread on the BBC report has no comments; Reddit not read. Main answer unchanged (Not established, unclear).

headline: DWP has taken some online services offline after a cyber incident; it says benefit and pension payments are not affected.
summary: New incident page. DWP's GOV.UK notice (s001, first published 08:11 GMT Nov 27) says it took some online services offline as a precaution after identifying a cyber incident affecting its systems, is working with the National Cyber Security Centre and the Government Cyber Coordination Centre, that regular benefit and pension payments are not affected, and that it never messages people asking for bank details. The BBC (s002, a Press Association report) says that around 9 AM GMT the online systems for pensions, Universal Credit and PIP applications and Tell Us Once could not be accessed, and that DWP has not said what type of incident it is or whether personal data was accessed; The Register (s003) reports the same statement and that officials have not said whether data was compromised; City AM (s004) reports Universal Credit sign-in problems. About line from DWP's GOV.UK page (s005). Main answer Not established, filed under unclear: DWP has not said that anyone got in. incident_type outage; service down on c002. Size Large. Picture: a Wikimedia Commons photograph of the Adelphi building (CC BY-SA 2.0), cropped to leave out passers-by, captioned as not a place involved. Theory sweep: one Hacker News thread with no comments; Reddit could not be read. Privacy check done: no staff, reporters or contact details named.
